newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco sees Dutch company purchase in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco sees Dutch company purchase in first quarter.

text.p: Tenneco Packaging, a unit of Tenneco Inc., said Thursday it was in talks to buy a Dutch maker of flexible packaging and expected to strike a deal by the end of the first quarter.

"The details on the internal structure (of the post-acquisition company) haven't been completely worked out yet," said Warren Hazelton, a spokesman for Evanston, Ill.-based Tenneco Packaging, "But we hope to reach an agreement in the first quarter."
Hazelton added the agreement's financial terms have yet to be determined.

Tenneco said it was holding exclusive talks to acquire the plastic packaging operation of NV Koninklijke KNP BT. The division, which posts annual sales of $550 million and has about 3,000 employees worldwide, makes plastic bubble wrap, polyethylene foam sheets and padded mailers.
"This deal gives us an entry into the flexible packaging business through a well-established, significant European company," Hazelton said.
He added there are no duplications between the divisions and no layoffs or staff reductions are planned.
Tenneco Packaging has spent $1.6 billion in the last two years buying speciality packaging businesses. The company currently posts annual sales of $4 billion.
